questions.q: What does LVL stand for?
questions.ref: APA - The Engineered Wood Association, engineered wood product terminology
questions.n: LVL is structural composite lumber made from bonded wood veneers with grain primarily oriented along the member length.

questions.q: What does the lumber designation S4S mean?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: S4S is the standard lumber abbreviation for material surfaced on all four sides.

questions.q: What is the gross area of one face of the partition?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - lumber, board-foot, partition and plywood quantity estimating
questions.n: Area is width multiplied by height: 5.80 × 2.80 = 16.24 m².
questions.scenario: A stud partition is 5.80 m long and 2.80 m high, framed with 2 in × 3 in lumber in 10 ft lengths and sheathed on both faces with 1.20 m × 2.40 m plywood.

questions.q: A wide board cups noticeably as its moisture content changes. Which wood characteristic explains why shrinkage is not equal in all directions?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Wood movement differs in tangential, radial, and longitudinal directions, so unequal dimensional change can produce distortion.

questions.q: Which treatment category is intended to improve wood resistance to decay or insects by forcing preservative into the material?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Pressure treatment drives preservative chemicals into wood, improving biological durability.

questions.q: Which sawing orientation is generally selected when dimensional stability and reduced distortion are priorities?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Quarter-sawn lumber has growth-ring orientation that generally improves dimensional stability across the board face relative to plain-sawn material.

questions.q: What is the vertical framing member of a stile-and-rail door called?
questions.ref: Architectural Woodwork Institute (AWI), Glossary and ANSI/AWI woodwork standards
questions.n: AWI defines stiles as the vertical members and rails as the horizontal members of a stile-and-rail assembly.

questions.q: A wall face measures 4.80 m by 2.40 m. How many 1.20 m by 2.40 m plywood sheets are required for one face, ignoring waste?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - lumber, board-foot, partition and plywood quantity estimating
questions.n: The wall area is 11.52 m² and each sheet covers 2.88 m², so exactly four sheets are required.

questions.q: What is the Bethell process?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: The Bethell process is the full-cell pressure process used to impregnate wood with preservative.

questions.q: Which of the following is a panel product rather than structural composite lumber used as dimension-type members?
questions.ref: APA - The Engineered Wood Association, engineered wood product terminology
questions.n: OSB is a structural wood panel; LVL, PSL, and LSL are structural composite lumber products.

questions.q: What board-foot quantity corresponds to 24 pieces of nominal 2 in × 3 in × 10 ft lumber?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - lumber, board-foot, partition and plywood quantity estimating
questions.n: Each piece contains 5 board feet; 24 pieces therefore total 120 board feet.

questions.q: Which hinge arrangement permits a service door to swing in both directions and return by gravity?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - carpentry and building-construction terminology
questions.n: Double-acting gravity hinges are used where a door must swing both ways, such as between food-service spaces.

questions.q: Using a factor of 8.060 bd ft/m², what estimated framing quantity results?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - lumber, board-foot, partition and plywood quantity estimating
questions.n: The tabular estimate is 16.24 × 8.060 = 130.89 board feet, or about 131 board feet.
questions.scenario: A stud partition is 5.80 m long and 2.80 m high, framed with 2 in × 3 in lumber in 10 ft lengths and sheathed on both faces with 1.20 m × 2.40 m plywood.

questions.q: Using a direct framing count, how many 10 ft pieces of 2 in × 3 in lumber should be allowed for the partition framing?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - lumber, board-foot, partition and plywood quantity estimating
questions.n: Counting the vertical studs and horizontal nailers gives a total framing length that requires 24 pieces of 10 ft stock after whole-piece rounding.
questions.scenario: A stud partition is 5.80 m long and 2.80 m high, framed with 2 in × 3 in lumber in 10 ft lengths and sheathed on both faces with 1.20 m × 2.40 m plywood.

questions.q: Which term describes lumber whose moisture content has been reduced by controlled heating in a drying chamber?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Kiln drying removes moisture under controlled temperature, humidity, and airflow conditions.

questions.q: What is the horizontal framing member of a stile-and-rail door called?
questions.ref: Architectural Woodwork Institute (AWI), Glossary and ANSI/AWI woodwork standards
questions.n: In stile-and-rail construction, rails are the horizontal members.

questions.q: Why is lumber seasoned before installation?
o: To limit shrinking and swelling in use
To make the wood fully waterproof
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Proper drying and moisture control reduce later shrinkage, swelling, distortion, and related service problems.

questions.q: What does PSL stand for?
questions.ref: APA - The Engineered Wood Association, engineered wood product terminology
questions.n: PSL is an engineered structural composite lumber product made from bonded wood strands oriented primarily parallel to the member length.

questions.q: How many board feet are contained in twelve pieces of nominal 2 in × 4 in × 10 ft lumber?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - lumber, board-foot, partition and plywood quantity estimating
questions.n: Each piece contains 2×4×10/12 = 6.667 board feet; twelve pieces contain 80 board feet.

questions.q: What type of joint commonly receives glazing at the edge of a wood sash or frame?
questions.ref: Architectural Woodwork Institute (AWI), Glossary and ANSI/AWI woodwork standards
questions.n: A rabbet provides a recessed seat along the edge of a sash or frame for glazing and associated glazing materials.

questions.q: Which shrinkage direction is generally greatest in ordinary wood?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: The USDA Wood Handbook reports tangential shrinkage as generally greater than radial shrinkage, while longitudinal shrinkage is much smaller.

questions.q: A cabinet door binds during a humid season but fits normally during drier months. What is the most direct material explanation?
o: The wood underwent only longitudinal shrinkage
The wood absorbed moisture and swelled
The wood lost all bound water
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Wood gains moisture from humid air and swells below the fiber-saturation range; cross-grain movement can change clearances.

questions.q: How many 1.20 m × 2.40 m plywood sheets are needed to cover both faces, before adding a waste allowance?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - lumber, board-foot, partition and plywood quantity estimating
questions.n: Both faces total 32.48 m². One sheet covers 2.88 m², so 32.48/2.88 = 11.28 sheets and the count rounds up to 12.
questions.scenario: A stud partition is 5.80 m long and 2.80 m high, framed with 2 in × 3 in lumber in 10 ft lengths and sheathed on both faces with 1.20 m × 2.40 m plywood.

questions.q: What term describes a material whose properties vary with direction?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Wood is anisotropic because properties differ in the longitudinal, radial, and tangential directions.

questions.q: What is a rabbet?
o: A projecting tongue on an edge
A round hole through a member
A rectangular recess along an edge
questions.ref: Architectural Woodwork Institute (AWI), Glossary and ANSI/AWI woodwork standards
questions.n: AWI defines a rabbet as a rectangular edge cut having two surfaces that form an L-shaped recess.

questions.q: A glue-laminated timber column is best classified as what general column type?
questions.ref: American Wood Council, National Design Specification and wood construction terminology
questions.n: Glulam members are manufactured by bonding multiple wood laminations into a larger structural member, making the column a built-up wood member.

questions.q: Which handheld high-speed rotary tool is used for profiling edges, cutting grooves, and shaping wood?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - carpentry and building-construction terminology
questions.n: A router is a high-speed rotary cutting tool used for shaping, profiling, and grooving wood.

questions.q: What generally happens to wood dimensions as it gains moisture below the fiber-saturation range?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Wood is hygroscopic; increasing bound-water content causes dimensional expansion below the fiber-saturation range.

questions.q: Which shrinkage direction is normally the smallest?
questions.ref: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (2021), Chs. 3, 4, 6, 13
questions.n: Longitudinal shrinkage is typically only a small fraction of tangential and radial shrinkage.
